set.body:
Scope

Replace warning-driven continuous-modulator repair with explicit scientific policies attached to the term/covariate specification.

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MissingValuePolicy distinguishes at least Reject, ZeroContribution, DropFromTerm, and ImputeConstant with precise row/trial semantics.
- [ ] ZeroContribution retains the parent categorical event while assigning zero only to the modulator contribution.
- [ ] Centering distinguishes None, GrandMean, WithinRun, WithinFactor/cells, and At(value) where supported.
- [ ] Any orthogonalization is a separately named ordered policy; it never occurs merely to mimic an external package convention.
- [ ] Policies are validated before convolution, preserved in the compiled design, and reported through DesignAudit receipts with affected row/trial identities.
- [ ] Strict mode promotes prohibited repair to a typed error rather than only a console warning.
- [ ] All-nonfinite, partially nonfinite, constant, zero-variance, and empty-scope modulators have explicit outcomes.
- [ ] Centering and missingness are invariant to event-row permutation and respect run/cell boundaries.
- [ ] R parity fixtures identify intentional policy differences rather than silently applying R defaults.
- [ ] JVM and Scala.js tests cover every policy and receipt.
set.title: P2.2: make modulator missingness, centering, and orthogonalization explicit
